title: Inefficiencies in Local Infrastructure: Evidence from Drinking Water in California
abstract: Local elected officials oversee critical infrastructure, often with limited electoral accountability. This paper studies how this distorts investment across California drinking-water systems. We document that pollution responds to shifts in the political environment, motivating a dynamic model of public investment. We measure welfare returns to investment directly, combining event-study estimates of investment effectiveness and costs with those of residents’ clean-water valuations, recovered from housing choices. Investment choices identify policymakers’ responsiveness to those returns. Weak accountability diverts investment from high-return systems and conventional policies imperfectly offset these distortions: subsidy takeup is misaligned with returns, while uniform mandates induce welfare losses. Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.
abstract_zh: 地方民选官员负责监督关键基础设施，但其选举问责往往有限。本文研究了这一问题如何扭曲加利福尼亚州饮用水系统的投资。我们记录到，污染随政治环境的变化而变化，由此建立了一个公共投资的动态模型。我们直接衡量投资的福利回报，将投资有效性和成本的事件研究估计，与通过住房选择推断出的居民清洁水资源估值相结合。投资选择可以识别政策制定者对这些回报的响应程度。薄弱的问责机制使投资从高回报系统转移出去，而常规政策只能不完善地抵消这些扭曲：补贴的领取与回报不匹配，而统一的强制性规定则导致福利损失。美国国家经济研究局（NBER）工作论文系列的机构订阅者以及发展中国家的居民可免费从www.nber.org下载本文。

Policy Influence and Private Returns from Lobbying in the Energy Sector
abstract: Firms lobby the U.S. Congress to influence policy-making. This paper quantifies the extent to which lobbying expenditures affect policy enactment. First, I construct a novel dataset comprised of federal energy legislation and lobbying activities by the energy sector during the 110th Congress. Second, I develop and estimate a game- theoretic model where heterogeneous players choose lobbying expenditures to affect the probability that a policy is enacted. I find that the effect of lobbying expenditures on a policy's equilibrium enactment probability is very small. However, the average returns from lobbying expenditures are estimated to be over 140%.
abstract_zh: 企业游说美国国会以影响政策制定。本文量化了游说支出在多大程度上影响政策的颁布。首先，我构建了一个新颖的数据集，包括第110届国会期间的联邦能源立法以及能源行业的游说活动。其次，我构建并估计了一个博弈论模型，其中异质性参与者选择游说支出，以影响某项政策被颁布的概率。我发现，游说支出对政策均衡颁布概率的影响非常小。然而，据估计，游说支出的平均回报率超过140%。
